stories.titleEn: Supreme and Elliott Smith: Album Covers in a Thursday Drop
stories.zhDeck: Supreme 这周的上新把一位独立音乐人的唱片封面和照片带到了衣服上。品牌 11 月 9 日发布消息，宣布与 Elliott Smith 遗产管理方获准合作的秋季系列：一件工装夹克、一件连帽卫衣、一件保暖上衣、三款 T 恤和一顶针织帽。系列将于 11 月 12 日在欧美发售，亚洲日期为 11 月 14 日。[Modern Notoriety 报道](https://modernnotoriety.com/supreme-elliott-smith-release-date/)
stories.enDeck: A Supreme collection uses imagery associated with the musician.
stories.zhMarkdown:
Supreme 这周的上新把一位独立音乐人的唱片封面和照片带到了衣服上。品牌 11 月 9 日发布消息，宣布与 Elliott Smith 遗产管理方获准合作的秋季系列：一件工装夹克、一件连帽卫衣、一件保暖上衣、三款 T 恤和一顶针织帽。系列将于 11 月 12 日在欧美发售，亚洲日期为 11 月 14 日。[Modern Notoriety 报道](https://modernnotoriety.com/supreme-elliott-smith-release-date/)

衣服上的图像对应 Smith 不同阶段的音乐。联名上衣采用《Figure 8》的封面照片；一件 T 恤对应《Either/Or》，另一件借用了 1995 年同名专辑的视觉。夹克和帽子出现《XO》字样。服饰媒体 Modern Notoriety 报道，《Figure 8》封面照片由 Autumn de Wilde 拍摄；另一款 Mask Tee 使用 Deb Pastor 的摄影作品。[系列单品](https://modernnotoriety.com/supreme-elliott-smith-release-date/) · [JustFresh 设计细节](https://www.justfresh.co/music/supreme-elliott-smith-fall-2026-collection)

摄影并不只是这次联名的装饰。de Wilde 在 Pitchfork 2013 年的口述史中回忆，拍摄《Figure 8》时，Smith 曾说他喜欢色彩，不想总在照片里被呈现得阴暗。摄影师后来选取洛杉矶街头一面彩色墙作为拍摄背景；这张照片也成为这张唱片的视觉入口。[Pitchfork 口述史](https://pitchfork.com/features/article/9246-keep-the-things-you-forgot-an-elliott-smith-oral-history/) · [LA Weekly 对摄影师的采访](https://www.laweekly.com/chasing-the-light-emma-director-autumn-de-wilde-brings-vibrant-beauty-to-film/)

Smith 本人早年也谈过这种被简化的形象。在一次围绕《Figure 8》的采访里，他说歌曲表达的感受不必被理解为创作者每时每刻的状态；他也讲到请朋友 de Wilde 执导《Son of Sam》录像，是因为他喜欢并尊重她的摄影。这些话有助于理解旧作品的背景，但不能用来判断他会如何看待 2026 年的联名。[In Music We Trust 采访](https://www.inmusicwetrust.com/articles/34h03.html)

媒体对新系列的反应并不一致。Pitchfork 对联名的设计和商业化表达了明确质疑；Stereogum 的 Tom Breihan 同样对用潮牌服饰表达喜爱持保留态度。另一边，Rolling Stone Canada 的 Jeff Ihaza 认为，Smith 的音乐与滑板文化有长期关联，Supreme 与音乐人合作也并非第一次。这些都是评论者的观点，不代表所有乐迷的看法。[Pitchfork 评论](https://pitchfork.com/story/a-supreme-elliott-smith-collection-what-the-hell-sure/) · [Stereogum 评论](https://stereogum.com/2517109/supreme-announces-elliott-smith-collection/news) · [Rolling Stone Canada](https://ca.rollingstone.com/music/elliott-smith-supreme-collab-controversy/)

如果从音乐本身入手，《Either/Or》和《Figure 8》也值得重听。Pitchfork 对《Either/Or》再版的评论关注了它如何在亲密的低音量演唱与更丰富的编曲之间移动；WFAE 转载的 NPR 采访中，音乐人回看《Figure 8》时，也谈到了过去围绕独立音乐人签约大厂的争论。Stereogum 的 Lindsey Rhoades 在专辑二十周年评论中注意到《Figure 8》的明亮旋律与更复杂情绪之间的张力。这些历史讨论为现在的联名提供了背景，却无法替当事人回答未曾说过的话。[Either/Or 乐评](https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/22947-eitheror-expanded-edition/) · [WFAE 采访](https://www.wfae.org/2020-04-16/learning-from-elliott-smith-20-years-after-figure-8) · [Stereogum 二十周年乐评](https://stereogum.com/2080262/elliott-smith-figure-8-review-2000/reviews/the-anniversary)

对照当年的评论与后来的回望，还能听到这些唱片的不同层次。Sara Marcus 在 1997 年为《Oberlin Review》写的《Either/Or》评论，一边欣赏指弹与多轨人声，一边认为部分更厚重的鼓声需要时间适应。Sam Sodomsky 在 2020 年回看 1995 年同名专辑时，则注意到简约录音中细致叠加的声音。Smith 在 2000 年接受 Hot Press 采访时，谈到《Figure 8》中对钢琴的使用和在 Abbey Road 录音的经历。三篇都是对旧唱片与创作的讨论，并非对本次联名的评价。[Oberlin Review](https://www2.oberlin.edu/stupub/ocreview/archives/1997.03.28/arts/smith.html) · [Pitchfork 同名专辑乐评](https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/elliott-smith-elliott-smith/) · [Hot Press 旧访谈](https://www.hotpress.com/music/on-this-day-in-2000-elliott-smith-released-figure-8-23138147)

发售时间方面，Supreme 公告公布了日期，没有给出具体时刻。独立追踪网站 Supreme Drop List 写美国东部时间 11 月 12 日上午 11 点，对应北京时间 11 月 13 日零点；这不是品牌对本次亚洲发售时间的确认。具体价格和地区库存仍以官方最终上架为准。[Supreme Drop List](https://supremedroplist.com/news/supreme-turns-the-volume-down-for-fw26-week-13-with-elliott-smith)

1997 年，《BOMB》在《Either/Or》发行当年注意到封面照片里 Smith 手臂上的公牛纹身，并描述他在波特兰家中弹奏、混录不同乐器。那是作品刚出来时的一份观察；今天衣服上的封面，也可以成为重新打开唱片、回到这些具体细节的入口。[BOMB 乐评](https://bombmagazine.org/articles/1997/10/01/elliott-smiths-either-or/)
stories.enMarkdown:
Supreme’s latest weekly drop brings the covers and photographs associated with an independent musician onto clothing. On November 9, the brand announced a fall collection made with permission from the Estate of Elliott Smith: a work jacket, hooded sweatshirt, thermal, three T-shirts and a beanie. Supreme gives November 12 as the release date and November 14 for Asia. [Modern Notoriety report](https://modernnotoriety.com/supreme-elliott-smith-release-date/)

The images refer to different stages of Smith’s recording career. The thermal uses imagery from the cover of *Figure 8*; other shirts refer to *Either/Or* and the 1995 self-titled album. The jacket and beanie carry the letters *XO*. Fashion publication Modern Notoriety identifies Autumn de Wilde as the photographer of the *Figure 8* cover and Deb Pastor as the photographer behind the Mask Tee. [Collection details](https://modernnotoriety.com/supreme-elliott-smith-release-date/) · [JustFresh](https://www.justfresh.co/music/supreme-elliott-smith-fall-2026-collection)

Photography was more than decoration in the original work. In a 2013 Pitchfork oral history, de Wilde recalled that Smith wanted his pictures to move beyond a persistently dark portrayal and that he loved colour. The photographer chose a colourful Los Angeles wall as a setting; the image became a visual entry point to the album. [Pitchfork oral history](https://pitchfork.com/features/article/9246-keep-the-things-you-forgot-an-elliott-smith-oral-history/) · [LA Weekly interview](https://www.laweekly.com/chasing-the-light-emma-director-autumn-de-wilde-brings-vibrant-beauty-to-film/)

Smith himself had discussed the limits of that simplified image. In an interview around *Figure 8*, he said the feelings in songs should not be assumed to describe a writer’s every moment. He also explained that he asked his friend de Wilde to direct the “Son of Sam” video because he liked and respected her photographs. Those remarks help explain the earlier work; they do not tell us what he would have thought of a collaboration in 2026. [In Music We Trust interview](https://www.inmusicwetrust.com/articles/34h03.html)

Responses to the collection differ. Pitchfork criticised the designs and the commercial gesture, while Stereogum’s Tom Breihan expressed reservations about celebrating Smith through streetwear. Rolling Stone Canada’s Jeff Ihaza took the opposite view, pointing to Smith’s history within skate culture and Supreme’s long record of working with musicians. These are individual critical responses, not a verdict shared by all listeners. [Pitchfork](https://pitchfork.com/story/a-supreme-elliott-smith-collection-what-the-hell-sure/) · [Stereogum](https://stereogum.com/2517109/supreme-announces-elliott-smith-collection/news) · [Rolling Stone Canada](https://ca.rollingstone.com/music/elliott-smith-supreme-collab-controversy/)

The records themselves offer another route in. Pitchfork’s review of the *Either/Or* reissue attends to the movement between hushed intimacy and more expansive arrangements. In an interview for NPR member station WFAE, a musician looking back at *Figure 8* also discussed older arguments about independent artists signing to major labels. In her twentieth-anniversary review, Stereogum’s Lindsey Rhoades heard tension between the album’s bright melodies and its more complicated emotions. These earlier conversations add context without speaking for Smith on the present release. [Either/Or review](https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/22947-eitheror-expanded-edition/) · [WFAE interview](https://www.wfae.org/2020-04-16/learning-from-elliott-smith-20-years-after-figure-8) · [Stereogum anniversary review](https://stereogum.com/2080262/elliott-smith-figure-8-review-2000/reviews/the-anniversary)

Contemporary criticism and later listening reveal different layers in those records. In a 1997 review of *Either/Or* for the *Oberlin Review*, Sara Marcus admired the fingerpicking and layered voices while finding some of its heavier drumming took time to absorb. Looking back at the 1995 self-titled album in 2020, Sam Sodomsky heard intricate layers inside its spare recordings. In a 2000 Hot Press interview, Smith discussed his use of piano on *Figure 8* and his experience recording at Abbey Road. All three concern the earlier music and its making; none is a response to this collaboration. [Oberlin Review](https://www2.oberlin.edu/stupub/ocreview/archives/1997.03.28/arts/smith.html) · [Pitchfork review](https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/elliott-smith-elliott-smith/) · [Hot Press interview](https://www.hotpress.com/music/on-this-day-in-2000-elliott-smith-released-figure-8-23138147)

Supreme’s announcement gives dates but no specific launch time. Independent tracker Supreme Drop List lists November 12 at 11 a.m. US Eastern time, which is midnight at the start of November 13 in Beijing; that is not an official time for the Asian release. Prices and regional stock should be checked against the final official listings. [Supreme Drop List](https://supremedroplist.com/news/supreme-turns-the-volume-down-for-fw26-week-13-with-elliott-smith)

Writing in 1997, BOMB noticed the bull tattoo on Smith’s arm on the *Either/Or* cover and described him playing and mixing several instruments at home in Portland. It is a view from the year the record appeared. The cover on a piece of clothing can also lead back to the album and its particular details. [BOMB review](https://bombmagazine.org/articles/1997/10/01/elliott-smiths-either-or/)

stories.title: ART021 上海：李昢的镜面雕塑与破碎的未来
stories.titleEn: Lee Bul’s Mirrored Sculpture at ART021 Shanghai
stories.zhDeck: ART021 上海廿一当代艺术博览会上，豪瑟沃斯将展位留给李昢的一件作品：《Untitled Sculpture (W3)》（2010）。画廊公布的展位是 C05，展期为 11 月 11 日至 14 日。它将镜面和破碎般的建筑形体组合在一起，观众的影像也在反射中被切开、重组。这里关于上海展位的资料来自画廊公布的信息，并非我们对现场的观察。[豪瑟沃斯](https://www.hauserwirth.com/zh-Hant/art-fairs/art021-2026/)
stories.enDeck: Hauser & Wirth presents one work by the artist at the Shanghai fair.
stories.zhMarkdown:
ART021 上海廿一当代艺术博览会上，豪瑟沃斯将展位留给李昢的一件作品：《Untitled Sculpture (W3)》（2010）。画廊公布的展位是 C05，展期为 11 月 11 日至 14 日。它将镜面和破碎般的建筑形体组合在一起，观众的影像也在反射中被切开、重组。这里关于上海展位的资料来自画廊公布的信息，并非我们对现场的观察。[豪瑟沃斯](https://www.hauserwirth.com/zh-Hant/art-fairs/art021-2026/)

博览会位于上海展览中心：11 月 11 日和 12 日为贵宾及藏家预览，13 日和 14 日向公众开放。若计划前往，建议以主办方公布的入场信息为准。[白石画廊发布的博览会信息](https://www.whitestone-gallery.com/zh-hans/blogs/art-fair/art021-2026)

《W3》不是为这次上海展位新制作的作品。它早在 2018 年伦敦海沃德画廊的个展中展出；当时的图片记录将它与《Titan》（2013）并列。回到上海看这件 2010 年的雕塑，有意思的地方正在于：它带着过往展览中积累的语境进入一场当代艺博会，而不是只作为一件闪亮的新奇物出现。[海沃德／Google Arts 访谈](https://artsandculture.google.com/story/lee-bul-on-the-inspiration-behind-her-futuristic-show-at-the-hayward-gallery/hwVhN08P4tphIA?hl=en) · [The Spaces 2018 报道](https://thespaces.com/lee-bul-transforms-londons-hayward-gallery-into-a-sci-fi-playground/)

画廊将《W3》视为 Sternbau 系列的一个变体。理解这条线索，可以回看李昢更早的建筑式雕塑：2009 年 Thaddaeus Ropac 的展览文字提到，艺术家借由 Bruno Taut 对玻璃、轻盈和透明性的想象，思考一个被建筑构想出来的理想世界。这并不意味着《W3》是对某张建筑图纸的直接复制；它把建筑愿景转成一种不稳定的空间经验。[Ropac 2009 展览说明](https://ropac.net/de/exhibitions/335-lee-bul-drawings/)

镜子在这里也不是单纯用来增加亮度。豪瑟沃斯援引艺术家的想法：当熟悉的自我影像反复分裂，观看者还能否同样自然地认出自己？2018 年策展人 Stephanie Rosenthal 在另一场采访中谈到，李昢的镜面装置会扰乱人对空间的判断，让身体和感官参与观看。这是对艺术家实践的理解，具体体验仍取决于作品的现场呈现。[豪瑟沃斯](https://www.hauserwirth.com/zh-Hant/art-fairs/art021-2026/) · [SLEEK 策展人访谈](https://www.sleek-mag.com/article/lee-bul/)

这件作品也能放回她更长的创作脉络里。M+ 2026 年回顾展把建筑式装置、Cyborg 与 Anagram 系列、草图和模型并置；回顾展已于 8 月结束。艺术家在与 M+ 策展人 Doryun Chong 的对谈中说，她关心技术与权力，也花大量时间测试材料，并不急于把想法变成最终作品。展览资料中，豪瑟沃斯也是赞助方之一。[M+ 展览](https://www.mplus.org.hk/en/exhibitions/lee-bul-from-1998-to-now/) · [M+ 对谈](https://www.mplus.org.hk/en/magazine/lee-bul-and-doryun-chong-in-conversation/)

她对身体、建筑与未来的兴趣并未固定在一种形式。2024 年，大都会艺术博物馆委托她为纽约第五大道正立面制作四件雕塑；作家 R. O. Kwon 后来写下自己由远而近观看这些形体的感受：看似熟悉的轮廓靠近后又变得难以归类。2025 年《Observer》对首尔李昢回顾展的报道，则将工作室里的模型和反射空间放在一起理解。两者是历史背景，不是对上海展位的报道。[大都会博物馆 2024 资料](https://www.metmuseum.org/press-releases/facade-commission_lee-bul-2024-exhibitions) · [R. O. Kwon 的文章](https://www.metmuseum.org/ko/perspectives/escape-artist) · [Observer](https://observer.com/2025/10/artist-interview-lee-bul-grand-narrative-cryptic-interview-leeum-museum/)

策展人 Jiyoon Lee 在为另一场展览写的文章中，将艺术家对未实现未来的关注比作拆开结构、观察它如何组成。这个角度也适合带去看《W3》：欣赏镜面的精巧之后，再看看它如何让看似完整的空间和自我变得碎裂。[Jiyoon Lee 策展文章](https://assets.ctfassets.net/y3wgx2ncas6t/53QnxWubLXvqbXtK5HhqeK/187f2a568c6c7a86cad2b9ade67a605d/CuratorialStatement_LeeBul_HWNY.pdf)
stories.enMarkdown:
At ART021 Shanghai, Hauser & Wirth is presenting a single work by Lee Bul: *Untitled Sculpture (W3)* (2010). The gallery lists booth C05 and dates of 11–14 November. Its mirrored, fractured architectural form multiplies and interrupts the viewer’s reflection. Details about the Shanghai presentation come from the gallery’s announcement; they are not based on our own visit. [Hauser & Wirth](https://www.hauserwirth.com/zh-Hant/art-fairs/art021-2026/)

The fair takes place at Shanghai Exhibition Center. According to another participating gallery, 11 and 12 November are VIP and collector preview days, followed by public days on 13 and 14 November. Check the organiser’s admission information before visiting. [Whitestone Gallery](https://www.whitestone-gallery.com/zh-hans/blogs/art-fair/art021-2026)

*W3* is not a new work made for Shanghai. It was shown at the Hayward Gallery in London in 2018, where an installation image records it alongside *Titan* (2013). Its return in an art-fair booth brings accumulated exhibition history into the present. [Hayward / Google Arts interview](https://artsandculture.google.com/story/lee-bul-on-the-inspiration-behind-her-futuristic-show-at-the-hayward-gallery/hwVhN08P4tphIA?hl=en) · [The Spaces](https://thespaces.com/lee-bul-transforms-londons-hayward-gallery-into-a-sci-fi-playground/)

The gallery describes *W3* as a variation on Lee’s Sternbau series. An earlier 2009 exhibition text connects related architectural sculptures to Bruno Taut’s visions of glass, lightness and transparency. This is a way into Lee’s thinking about imagined worlds, not evidence that *W3* directly reproduces a particular architectural plan. [Ropac](https://ropac.net/de/exhibitions/335-lee-bul-drawings/)

The mirrors do more than make the work gleam. The gallery quotes Lee asking what happens to recognition when a familiar self-image is repeatedly fragmented. In a separate 2018 interview, curator Stephanie Rosenthal described how Lee’s reflective environments disturb spatial perception and draw the body into the encounter. How this particular presentation feels remains a question for visitors. [Hauser & Wirth](https://www.hauserwirth.com/zh-Hant/art-fairs/art021-2026/) · [SLEEK](https://www.sleek-mag.com/article/lee-bul/)

This inquiry belongs to a longer practice. The 2026 M+ survey placed architectural installations alongside the *Cyborg* and *Anagram* series, drawings and models; the Hong Kong presentation ended in August. In conversation with curator Doryun Chong, Lee reflected on technology and power, and on the time she spends testing materials before completing a work. Hauser & Wirth was among the exhibition’s supporters. [M+ exhibition](https://www.mplus.org.hk/en/exhibitions/lee-bul-from-1998-to-now/) · [M+ conversation](https://www.mplus.org.hk/en/magazine/lee-bul-and-doryun-chong-in-conversation/)

Her interest in bodies, architecture and imagined futures takes different forms. In 2024, the Metropolitan Museum of Art commissioned four sculptures for its Fifth Avenue facade. Writer R. O. Kwon later described recognisable shapes becoming harder to classify as she approached them. An *Observer* report on the 2025 Leeum survey considered the artist’s models and reflective spaces together. Both are historical context, not reports from Shanghai. [The Met](https://www.metmuseum.org/press-releases/facade-commission_lee-bul-2024-exhibitions) · [R. O. Kwon](https://www.metmuseum.org/ko/perspectives/escape-artist) · [Observer](https://observer.com/2025/10/artist-interview-lee-bul-grand-narrative-cryptic-interview-leeum-museum/)

Writing for a separate exhibition, curator Jiyoon Lee describes an attention to unrealised futures as a way of opening up a structure and examining how its parts fit together. It is a useful prompt for encountering *W3*: after taking in its surfaces, look at what happens to the apparent coherence of space and self. [Jiyoon Lee’s curatorial statement](https://assets.ctfassets.net/y3wgx2ncas6t/53QnxWubLXvqbXtK5HhqeK/187f2a568c6c7a86cad2b9ade67a605d/CuratorialStatement_LeeBul_HWNY.pdf)

stories.zhMarkdown:
一盏纸灯可以同时是照明器具、可携带的手工制品和一件雕塑。纽约野口勇美术馆的《No Ordinary Light: Akari at 75》从 11 月 4 日展至 2027 年 9 月 5 日，把 Akari 七十五年的不同形态放回它们曾经出现的房间与展览之中。馆方介绍，野口勇自 1951 年起设计了 200 多种 Akari；这场展览还将纸灯与石、金属和陶土作品并置。[美术馆展览资料](https://www.artandobject.com/press-release/noguchi-museum-celebrates-isamu-noguchis-akari-light-sculptures) · [White Cube 展览介绍](https://www.whitecube.com/news/no-ordinary-light-akari-at-75-at-the-noguchi-museum)

故事开始于日本岐阜。美术馆的研究文章记录，1951 年春天，野口勇在长良川看到夜间鸬鹚捕鱼的船只，船上点着以桑树皮纸制作的灯笼。岐阜市长希望他帮助当地灯笼业寻找新的方向，于是邀请他参与设计。最初的实验并没有立即获得所有人的认可：馆方文章记载，当地报纸曾用“变形”来描述原型。[野口勇美术馆：Akari 历史](https://shop.noguchi.org/blogs/stories/history-of-akari-light-sculptures)

制作过程仍依靠岐阜工坊的手艺。制造商 Ozeki 介绍，工匠先组装木模，再沿模具的沟槽将竹条绕成螺旋，把和纸一条条贴上去，干燥之后取出木模。制造商解释，纸面自然形成的收缩与褶皱被有意保留，成为材料和工艺留下的形态。[Ozeki 工序](https://akari-ozeki.com/make/) · [Ozeki 材料介绍](https://www.ozeki-lantern.co.jp/en/akari.html)

不同型号之间的变化并不只是尺寸。Ozeki 对早期款式的说明提到紧密而均匀的竹骨、灯罩两端的木环，以及三脚或四脚细金属支架；之后的系列发展出悬吊、长条和更像蜘蛛腿的支撑方式。《Wallpaper*》采访美术馆工作人员时提到，9A 台灯和 14A 落地灯属于较早的款式，两者都有三脚支架。形式不同，纸和竹的轻薄感仍然留在作品里。[Ozeki 系列说明](https://www.ozeki-lantern.co.jp/en/akari.html) · [Wallpaper* 采访](https://www.wallpaper.com/design-interiors/lighting/isamu-noguchi-akari-history)

纸灯并不是野口勇第一次尝试让作品自己发光。纽约现代艺术博物馆 1977 年旧展资料介绍，他在 1940 年代制作过内部带灯泡的《Lunar》雕塑，也曾试验塑料和纸袋。亚特兰大 High Museum 最近一场关于他设计实践的展览，同样把这些早期实验与 Akari 联系起来：光源不是后来附加的装饰，而是雕塑自身的一部分。[MoMA 1977 年资料](https://www.moma.org/momaorg/shared/pdfs/docs/press_archives/5552/releases/MOMA_1977_0091_86.pdf) · [High Museum 旧展](https://high.org/exhibition/noguchi/)

灯也能改变它所在空间的尺度。纽约大都会艺术博物馆收藏的《Akari E》是一件约 1951 年设计的悬挂作品，馆方记录它高约 280 厘米，由桑树皮纸、竹和金属线构成。它属于大都会的收藏，不应误认作这次野口勇美术馆的展品；但它能帮助理解同一系列如何从桌边向房间延伸。[大都会艺术博物馆作品档案](https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/485657)

1986 年威尼斯双年展上，野口勇把灯与石头共同放进美国馆。2026 年巴黎 OGATA 与野口勇美术馆合作的旧展介绍了两款相关型号：三角形纸灯从上方悬挂，底部绳线连接包裹着和纸的石头。这种做法让灯不只占据天花板，也和地面产生关系；巴黎展示提供的是作品历史，不能代替本次纽约展的现场判断。[OGATA × 野口勇美术馆](https://ogata.com/paris/galerie/the-noguchi-museum-natures-way-en/)

在纽约另一处正在进行的展示里，Akari 又进入了办公楼。建筑事务所 SOM 介绍，野口勇曾与建筑师 Gordon Bunshaft 为 Lever House 庭院构思两项最终未实现的方案；今年的展示将他的雕塑、模型和图纸带回广场与大厅，并在大厅陈列 Akari。建筑杂志《Architect》讨论亚特兰大另一场回顾展时也指出，他的灯具、家具和公共空间设计不应被当作雕塑之外的次要工作。这些都是不同展览提供的背景，不是本次美术馆展厅的现场描述。[SOM 的 Lever House 展示](https://www.som.com/news/lever-house-celebrates-its-75th-anniversary-with-isamu-noguchi-exhibition/) · [Architect 文章](https://www.architectmagazine.com/design/this-exhibition-changes-how-we-talk-about-design/)

皮博迪埃塞克斯博物馆在另一场展览的策展人访谈中谈到，野口勇的作品通过杂志、目录和百货商店进入家庭。他并未只为一个固定场景设计：同一盏灯既可能出现在现代主义室内，也能与木质家具共同生活。今天重看 Akari，值得留意的不只是它熟悉的轮廓，还有岐阜工匠怎样让一张纸、一根竹条和一个灯泡共同形成空间。[Peabody Essex Museum 策展人访谈](https://www.pem.org/blog/curator-q-a-behind-the-scenes-of-isamu-noguchi-i-am-not-a-designer)
stories.enMarkdown:
A paper light can be an illumination device, a portable handmade object and a sculpture at once. *No Ordinary Light: Akari at 75*, at New York’s Noguchi Museum from November 4 through September 5, 2027, returns Akari to the rooms and exhibitions in which its many forms appeared. The museum says Isamu Noguchi designed more than 200 Akari from 1951 onward; the exhibition also places paper lights in conversation with works in stone, metal and clay. [Museum exhibition material](https://www.artandobject.com/press-release/noguchi-museum-celebrates-isamu-noguchis-akari-light-sculptures) · [White Cube](https://www.whitecube.com/news/no-ordinary-light-akari-at-75-at-the-noguchi-museum)

The story begins in Gifu, Japan. In spring 1951, the museum’s historical account records, Noguchi saw cormorant-fishing boats on the Nagara River illuminated by lanterns made from mulberry-bark paper. Gifu’s mayor asked him to help find a new direction for the city’s lantern trade. The early experiments did not win everyone over immediately: the museum notes that a local newspaper described the prototypes as “deformed.” [Noguchi Museum history](https://shop.noguchi.org/blogs/stories/history-of-akari-light-sculptures)

Making Akari still depends on the skills of the Gifu workshop. Manufacturer Ozeki describes assembling a wooden mould, winding a bamboo strip through its grooves, then pasting washi paper over the frame. When the paper dries, the mould is removed. The manufacturer explains that natural shrinkage and wrinkles in the paper are deliberately preserved as part of the sculpture’s material character. [Ozeki process](https://akari-ozeki.com/make/) · [Ozeki on materials](https://www.ozeki-lantern.co.jp/en/akari.html)

The differences between models are not simply a matter of size. Ozeki identifies tightly spaced bamboo ribs and wooden collars in early models, alongside slender three- or four-legged metal bases; later series developed into suspended, elongated and spider-legged forms. In an interview with *Wallpaper*, museum staff identify the 9A table light and 14A floor light as early models, both with three-legged supports. The shapes change, but the lightness of paper and bamboo remains. [Ozeki series](https://www.ozeki-lantern.co.jp/en/akari.html) · [Wallpaper interview](https://www.wallpaper.com/design-interiors/lighting/isamu-noguchi-akari-history)

Akari was not Noguchi’s first attempt to make an object emit its own light. Material for a 1977 exhibition at the Museum of Modern Art describes his internally illuminated *Lunar* sculptures of the 1940s and later experiments with plastic and a paper bag. A recent High Museum exhibition also connects those early experiments with Akari: illumination was not merely an accessory added afterwards, but part of the sculpture itself. [MoMA 1977 release](https://www.moma.org/momaorg/shared/pdfs/docs/press_archives/5552/releases/MOMA_1977_0091_86.pdf) · [High Museum exhibition](https://high.org/exhibition/noguchi/)

The lights can also change the scale of the spaces they occupy. The Metropolitan Museum of Art’s *Akari E*, designed around 1951, is a hanging work approximately 280 centimetres high, made of mulberry-bark paper, bamboo and wire. It belongs to the Met’s collection and should not be mistaken for a work in the present Noguchi Museum show. It does, however, show how the series could extend from a tabletop into a room. [Metropolitan Museum object record](https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/485657)

At the 1986 Venice Biennale, Noguchi placed lights and stones together in the United States Pavilion. For a separate 2026 presentation in Paris, OGATA and the Noguchi Museum described two related models: triangular shades hang overhead, with cords at their bases tied to stones wrapped in washi. The light connects ceiling and floor. That Paris presentation provides historical context, not a first-hand account of the current New York installation. [OGATA and the Noguchi Museum](https://ogata.com/paris/galerie/the-noguchi-museum-natures-way-en/)

At another ongoing presentation in New York, Akari enters an office building. Architecture firm SOM recounts two courtyard proposals Noguchi developed with architect Gordon Bunshaft for Lever House that were never realised; this year’s display brings his sculptures, models and drawings back to the plaza and lobby, with Akari in the lobby. Writing about a separate Atlanta survey, Architect magazine argues that lighting, furniture and public-space design should not be treated as secondary to his sculpture. Both are contexts from other exhibitions, not first-hand observations of the current museum show. [SOM on Lever House](https://www.som.com/news/lever-house-celebrates-its-75th-anniversary-with-isamu-noguchi-exhibition/) · [Architect article](https://www.architectmagazine.com/design/this-exhibition-changes-how-we-talk-about-design/)

In an interview for another exhibition, a Peabody Essex Museum curator describes Noguchi’s work entering homes through magazines, catalogues and department stores. He did not design for one fixed setting: the same light could appear in a modernist room or alongside natural wood. Looking at Akari today means noticing not only its familiar silhouette, but also how Gifu makers bring paper, bamboo and a bulb together to shape a space. [Peabody Essex curator interview](https://www.pem.org/blog/curator-q-a-behind-the-scenes-of-isamu-noguchi-i-am-not-a-designer)
